posts.title: The Salesforce Org in 3 Slides
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

One org, everything in it

Your org is one tenant on shared infrastructure \u2014 its own data, its own metadata, its own users.

  • Sandboxes are copies of the metadata, not the data
  • A Developer Edition is a free standalone org \u2014 your lab
  • Almost everything starts from Setup: learn the Quick Find box first
"}, {"type": "horizontalrule", "version": 1}, {"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Metadata is the product

Objects, fields, layouts, flows, classes \u2014 everything you build is metadata, and metadata can move between orgs.

  • Data lives in records; behaviour lives in metadata
  • Deployments move metadata, never (normally) data
  • If you can't retrieve it with the CLI, ask what it really is
"}, {"type": "horizontalrule", "version": 1}, {"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Security decides what the table shows

Two users open the same list view and see different worlds \u2014 by design.

  • Profiles + permission sets: what you can do
  • Org-wide defaults + sharing: which records you can see
  • Field-level security: which columns exist for you

Next step: open your own org and check all three for one user.

"}], "direction": "ltr", "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}

posts.title: Governor Limits Survival Deck
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Limits are the platform's contract

Shared infrastructure means every transaction runs inside hard budgets. The good news: only a handful matter day to day.

"}, {"type": "horizontalrule", "version": 1}, {"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

100 SOQL queries

The one that catches everyone. A query inside a loop over 200 trigger records is 200 queries.

  • Query before the loop, into a Map by Id
  • Let the trigger handler own the queries, not the helpers
"}, {"type": "horizontalrule", "version": 1}, {"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

150 DML statements

Same shape, same fix: collect records into a list, one insert or update at the end.

"}, {"type": "horizontalrule", "version": 1}, {"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

CPU time: 10 seconds

The quiet one \u2014 it accumulates across every trigger, flow and process in the transaction.

  • Measure with debug logs before optimising anything
  • Move heavy work async: Queueable beats @future
"}], "direction": "ltr", "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
